candidates.source_name: EKR – Elektronikus Közbeszerzési Rendszer (public procedure search)
candidates.why_relevant: Hungary's mandatory end-to-end e-procurement platform. Every in-scope procedure (incl. bank/state-owned buyers acting as contracting authorities) is run here; the public procedure list exposes procedure subject, contracting authority and status, which is the entry point to ATM/POS/kiosk/card-personalisation tenders and their result stages.
candidates.access_status: public (search/browse without login; some documents may require registered login)
candidates.legal_status: official government system; public data of public interest (közérdekű adat)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled crawl of the public procedure list filtered by CPV and keyword; follow through to notice documents. Prefer the publikus JSON/document endpoints under /api/publikus/ over HTML scraping; throttle politely.
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query + snowball from EKR portal navigation
queries_used: ekr.gov.hu nyilvános eljárások keresése hirdetmények nyilvános adatok EKR API adatszolgáltatás

candidates.source_name: EKR – Eredménytájékoztató hirdetmények (contract award notice data download)
candidates.why_relevant: The single most on-point page for this cell: award-result notices ('eredménytájékoztató') state the winning bidder (nyertes ajánlattevő) and contract value — the explicit vendor-buyer pair. Appears to offer bulk/structured download rather than notice-by-notice reading.
candidates.legal_status: official publication mandated by Kbt. (2015. évi CXLIII. tv.)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic bulk download of award-notice export, then local filtering on CPV + keyword; store winner name, value, CA, date for rebid-cycle tracking.

candidates.why_relevant: Register of concluded public contracts and their modifications. Gives contract text/metadata beyond the award notice — duration, scope, amendments and extensions — which is what tells you when an ATM-fleet or POS contract actually comes up for rebid.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Keyword/CA-scoped crawl; diff on contract modifications to catch silent extensions.
queries_used: ekr.gov.hu nyilvános eljárások keresése hirdetmények nyilvános adatok EKR API adatszolgáltatás

candidates.source_name: Közbeszerzési Értesítő (Official Journal of the Public Procurement Authority)
candidates.why_relevant: The official gazette carrying all domestic (below-EU-threshold and national) procurement notices, published every working day and freely available. Below-threshold notices matter because many single-bank ATM/POS/kiosk lots never reach the TED threshold.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Fetch the daily signed PDF issue (predictable pattern https://www.kozbeszerzes.hu/media/issue/pdf/signed/KE-YYYY-NN_.pdf), OCR-free text extract, keyword+CPV filter, then dedupe against EKR records.

negative_findings.description: Hungarian-language searches for a concrete ATM operation/maintenance award notice naming a winning bidder ('ATM üzemeltetés eredménytájékoztató nyertes ajánlattevő') returned only generic EKR documentation, training vendors and legal texts — no individual award record.
negative_findings.result_summary: General-purpose web search does not index the interiors of EKR/Értesítő notices well; the notices are inside session-driven search UIs and daily PDF issues.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the collection method must be direct querying of the registers and PDF issues, not web search. Do not conclude such contracts are absent.

negative_findings.description: The Hungarian terms 'POS terminál' and 'kártyaszemélyesítés' as free-text queries are dominated by commercial acquirer/SZÉP-kártya marketing pages (OTP, MBH) rather than procurement records.
negative_findings.result_summary: Noisy terms; unusable alone as collection filters.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Flag 'POS terminál', 'bankkártya elfogadás' and 'automata' as noisy — they must be combined with CPV codes or restricted to the procurement domains.

negative_findings.description: No Hungarian public-procurement source was found that is specifically scoped to banking/payment technology as a category; the sector is only reachable via CPV codes and keyword filters across general-purpose registers.
negative_findings.result_summary: No vertical/banking-specific procurement portal exists for HU.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell's collection design must be filter-driven over general registers; there is no shortcut feed.

negative_findings.description: An EKR public API path was observed in search results (ekr.gov.hu/api/publikus/kozbeszerzesi-hirdetmenyek/{id}/dokumentum-letoltes) but no published API documentation, rate limits or terms-of-use page was located in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Endpoint pattern plausible; contract and legality of automated use unconfirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A documented API would make this cell cheap and robust; if none exists, plan for headless-browser collection and confirm ToS.

negative_findings.description: The KBA database is served via Oracle APEX with session identifiers embedded in the URL, and the CoRe public search (kereso-core.kozbeszerzes.hu) was not fetched in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Both recorded as unverified rather than dead; no failed-fetch verdict is claimed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Deep-link-based collection will break; requires session-aware or headless access. Liveness must be settled by the deterministic verification pass.

negative_findings.description: Commercial banks in Hungary are largely private entities and are therefore NOT contracting authorities under Kbt.; their ATM/POS vendor contracts do not appear in these registers at all.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only state-owned or state-controlled financial actors (MNB, Magyar Államkincstár, Magyar Posta, Diákhitel Központ, state-owned banks) publish.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sets a hard ceiling on this cell's coverage of the private banking market; other workstreams must cover commercial-bank vendor relationships.

coverage_gaps.description: No complete enumerated list yet of Hungarian state-owned or state-controlled financial-sector contracting authorities (beyond MNB, Magyar Államkincstár, Magyar Posta, Diákhitel Központ, MÁV) whose own disclosure pages should be monitored.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Query the 'Nyilvántartott ajánlatkérők' (registered contracting authorities) register on kozbeszerzes.hu and filter by financial/postal/transport activity to build the buyer roster.

coverage_gaps.description: The exact CPV code set for banking/payment technology in HU procurement is not yet fixed. Only CPV 30144200 (jegykiadó gépek) was confirmed by name; codes for ATMs, cash-handling, card personalisation and self-service kiosks remain to be pinned down.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Download the free CPV lists (khf.hu PDF, tender-ertesito.hu list) and reconcile against the official EU CPV vocabulary to build an authoritative filter set before any bulk collection.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor names in HU notices appear in inconsistent legal forms (Zrt./Kft./Nyrt., accented vs unaccented, Hungarian subsidiary vs group brand), which will fragment award counts.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Plan a normalisation step keyed on tax number/company registry number where notices carry it; consider Opentender's already-normalised supplier field as a cross-check.

coverage_gaps.description: Framework-agreement call-offs under the KEF centralised system may not generate individual public award notices, hiding the actual vendor-buyer pair for central-government payment/IT purchases.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Investigate whether KEF publishes call-off/consumption data or supplier catalogues publicly; if not, log as a structural blind spot and rely on the framework roster plus annual KEF reporting.

coverage_gaps.description: No confirmed Hungarian term set yet for 'card personalisation' and 'self-service banking kiosk' as they are actually written in procurement notices; the seed term 'kártyaszemélyesítés' returned no procurement hits.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Mine confirmed notice PDFs for the in-use phrasing (e.g. kártyagyártás, kártyaperszonalizáció, ügyfélhívó/önkiszolgáló terminál, bankjegykiadó automata, készpénzbefizető automata) and rebuild the glossary from observed text rather than from translation.

coverage_gaps.description: Historical depth is unassessed: EKR only became mandatory from 2018, so pre-2018 awards live in older Értesítő archives with a different structure.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Determine the earliest machine-readable year in each register and decide the backfill horizon needed for rebid-cycle analysis (typically 8-10 years for ATM fleet contracts).

brief: Hungary's public-procurement record for banking and payment technology is concentrated in three official layers: EKR (ekr.gov.hu) as the mandatory transaction platform, with dedicated public surfaces for procedure search, award notices (eredménytájékoztató) and a public contract register; the Közbeszerzési Hatóság estate (kozbeszerzes.hu) carrying the daily Közbeszerzési Értesítő gazette, notice search, KBA/CoRe registers and the Döntőbizottság remedy decisions; and TED for everything above EU threshold in structured form. The Döntőbizottság decisions are the sleeper asset in this cell — unlike award notices they name the losing challengers and quote technical specs and scores. Two structural limits shape everything: private commercial banks are not contracting authorities and so never appear here, and KEF framework call-offs can consummate central-government purchases without an individual award notice. Practical collection is filter-driven rather than source-driven, so the immediate blockers are taxonomic (fixing the CPV code set) and lexical (deriving real Hungarian notice phrasing from observed notices instead of translated seed terms), plus supplier-name normalisation before any award counting.
